speaker: peterperez
text: Thank you. Good morning, Chief Justice Carballito, Justice Torres, and Justice Merriman. May it please the court. Philip Caso was convicted in a trial tainted with multiple errors. Specifically, the trial court committed plain error when it admitted Exhibit 13 at trial. In order to convict Mr. Caso of distribution and possession of a Schedule II controlled substance, the government was required to prove as an essential element the existence of a Schedule II controlled substance. Exhibit 13 was the people's purported drug exhibit. In order to admit Exhibit 13, the people were required to present a witness who had personal knowledge regarding the exhibit and who would be able to satisfy the evidentiary foundations required by Rule 901. In the instant case, the people presented Officer Champion. Officer Champion testified, this was the dope that was seized off of Cheryl. Aside from the field test, this is consistent with what I know methamphetamine to look like. On the basis of this testimony, the people moved to admit Exhibit 13. The defense did not object, and the court admitted Exhibit 13. Plain error occurred because the court did not satisfy the requirements of Rule 602 and 901. Specifically, with respect to Officer Champion, he did not seize Exhibit 13. He was not present during its seizure. He did not receive it. He was not in the chain of custody. He did not field test it. He did not lab test it. He had no Rule 602 personal knowledge, and he was unable to establish a Rule 901 authentication. It's plain error- I'm just embarrassed.

But what we have here is Officer Champion who did not have any personal knowledge regarding some of the factors the court gave us guidance about, regarding how the recording system operated, regarding its working condition and pattern of maintenance, who was operating it, had access to it and maintained it, who archived the recordings, regarding the quality of the recordings and the means by which the recording was copied to the format received at trial.
